properties.description:
The shared server publishes `exe_fingerprint` — `size:mtime_nanos` of its executable at start — and a client compares it before attaching. Mismatch means SIGTERM the daemon, clear the rendezvous, elect a fresh one. Match means attach exactly as before.

THREE NEAR-MATCHES OFFERED AND ALL READ. `cap:the-server-knows-its-own-currency` is the DETECTION this does not replace; `fact:the-attach-path-checks-liveness-and-identity-but-never-version` is the MEASUREMENT of the hole; `chg:a-client-replaces-a-mismatched-server-instead-of-reporting-it` DATES the repair. This is the standing capability that keeps it from reopening.

DISTINCT FROM THE DETECTION IN THREE WAYS THAT MATTER. That one asks a server about ITSELF — "was my executable replaced under me" — by reading `/proc/self/exe` for a ` (deleted)` marker, and it REPORTS. This compares TWO independently published facts and ACTS. So it catches "I was freshly spawned from an old build", which introspection cannot see by construction; it works on macOS, where the `/proc` read fails and `served_by.stale` can only ever answer `unknown`; and it removes the skew rather than announcing it.

⭐ THE COMPARAND IS THE DESIGN, AND TWO CANDIDATES WERE REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT BEFORE THIS ONE. A version string tells two builds of one version apart NOT AT ALL — the case that cost a development session six cycles on 2026-08-29 had `0.42.0` on both sides all day. An inode is worse: `install -m 755` rewrites IN PLACE and keeps it, so an inode check would have missed the field report that prompted the work. Size and mtime move under an in-place rewrite AND under `cargo build`'s unlink-and-replace, measured on both paths.

🛑 ABSENT MEANS REPLACE, NOT MATCH. A daemon publishing no fingerprint predates this field and is old by construction — which is the state of every daemon running at the moment this ships.

🛑 AND IT REFUSES TO GUESS TWICE OVER. A process that cannot fingerprint itself attaches rather than killing a healthy daemon on no evidence. A SIGTERM that fails attaches anyway, loudly, naming the manual remedy — a session on a stale surface is degraded, a session with no design brain is stopped, and the first is the lesser harm.

⚠️ THE STANDING RISK: this can stop a daemon another session is mid-write against. `--stop-shared` accepts the same risk with a human choosing the moment; this takes the choice automatically, judged the lesser harm against six recorded instances of sessions writing through the wrong surface.
properties.name: A session attaches only to a server of its own build, and replaces one that is not
